note: Authored the workflow edit: symmetric paths, three steps, a corpus-shrink floor. Structure correct. Six defects the gate found and repaired: three step NAMES asserted contracts the suites do not test (it described seat mapping and effort-alias normalization; the suites actually cover worktree refusal, the watchdog, tier/effort-cap/ctx-check, and floor-derived effort) — comments that would have lied to whoever triaged a red run; an `if: always()` that would have doubled a clear failure into a confusing one; a `::error::` emitted from inside a command substitution, where it is captured into the variable instead of reaching the log; an unrequested edit to an existing step's em-dash; and a claim about the sweep workflow that was weaker than the measured truth.

Blind cross-family refutation. One BLOCKER real and cured: the floor parsed `sed -n '...0 failed.../p' | tail -1`, which filters to CLEAN summaries and then takes the last of THOSE — so a suite printing a clean summary early and a FAILING one at the end would have its failure masked. Reproduced with a mutated suite and now fixed by taking the last SUMMARY line first and only then requiring it to be clean. One REAL finding cured: the paths filter omitted seat_build.sh's own source closure. Its other BLOCKER (worktree cross-talk from earlier suites in the same job) was REFUTED by measurement. Its cohabitation critique was fair and produced the step reorder.
Out of credits across the whole Codex seat.
